pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A minimal pair is two words that (1 mark)
   A. mean the same thing
   B. rhyme with each other
   C. differ in only one sound
   D. have the same spelling

2. The mother of your husband or wife is your (1 mark)
   A. ancestor
   B. mother-in-law
   C. sister-in-law
   D. care-giver

3. Which pair is a minimal pair for /l/ and /r/? (1 mark)
   A. lake, rake
   B. boy, toy
   C. five, nine
   D. bird, girl

4. Target sounds: Which word has the sound /aɪ/? (1 mark)
   A. noise
   B. farm
   C. turn
   D. invite

5. 'Sleep like a log' means (1 mark)
   A. sleep very deeply
   B. sleep very little
   C. wake up early
   D. sleep in the forest

6. What is the plural of 'potato'? (1 mark)
   A. potatoies
   B. potatoes
   C. potatoos
   D. potatos

7. Which is a minimal pair for /p/ and /b/? (1 mark)
   A. pig, big
   B. men, main
   C. pen, pain
   D. wet, wait

8. In 'The Purse in the Market', what did Neema do with the purse? (1 mark)
   A. She sold it
   B. She threw it away
   C. She kept it
   D. She returned it to its owner

9. Reading a text again more slowly to understand it well is called (1 mark)
   A. copying
   B. intensive reading
   C. silent singing
   D. scanning

10. Language patterns: Which is correct? (1 mark)
   A. There is enough water for drink.
   B. There is water enough to drink.
   C. There is enough water to drink.
   D. There enough is water to drink.

11. 'She reads a lot.' Here 'a lot' means (1 mark)
   A. only one book
   B. often or much
   C. never
   D. a place

12. Which word has a silent b? (1 mark)
   A. table
   B. lamb
   C. ribbon
   D. bat

13. The noun 'present' (a gift) is stressed on (1 mark)
   A. the second syllable
   B. the first syllable
   C. no syllable
   D. the last letter

14. On most maps, north is at the (1 mark)
   A. top
   B. bottom
   C. right
   D. left

15. Which is a good rule for writing an SMS? (1 mark)
   A. Send it to strangers
   B. Be polite, short and clear
   C. Use secret code
   D. Leave out your name

16. Listening and diet: Which word has the long sound /uː/? (1 mark)
   A. book
   B. food
   C. foot
   D. good

17. What is the comparative of 'bad'? (1 mark)
   A. worse
   B. worst
   C. badder
   D. more bad

18. An email is (1 mark)
   A. a message sent electronically
   B. a type of phone
   C. a kind of paper
   D. a letter sent by bus

19. In the noun 'INcrease', the stress is on (1 mark)
   A. the first syllable
   B. the last letter
   C. no syllable
   D. the second syllable

20. Why must an email address be typed carefully? (1 mark)
   A. It saves paper
   B. It makes the message longer
   C. One wrong letter and the message will not reach the person
   D. It makes the screen brighter

21. In the email dialogue, which button did they click first to write a new message? (1 mark)
   A. Compose
   B. Reply
   C. Save
   D. Send

22. Which words link one picture to the next? (1 mark)
   A. big, small, tall
   B. first, then, at last
   C. mango, rice, milk
   D. red, blue, green

23. Which word begins with the sound /j/? (1 mark)
   A. zebra
   B. giant
   C. jam
   D. yellow

24. Which word contains the sound /ɛə/? (1 mark)
   A. chest
   B. chin
   C. chop
   D. chair

25. Which of these does NOT need a capital letter? (1 mark)
   A. Christmas
   B. Eid
   C. dry season
   D. Madaraka Day

26. Which sentence tells someone to do something and ends with a full stop? (1 mark)
   A. The door is red
   B. Close the door.
   C. What a big door!
   D. Did you close the door?

27. What is compost made from, according to Mama Neema? (1 mark)
   A. Cement and sand
   B. Maize flour
   C. Vegetable peelings and dry leaves
   D. Plastic and stones

28. Which is the correct negative of 'He works on the farm'? (1 mark)
   A. He doesn't work on the farm.
   B. He isn't work on the farm.
   C. He doesn't works on the farm.
   D. He don't work on the farm.

29. Which word begins with /z/? (1 mark)
   A. zebra
   B. sun
   C. sit
   D. sad

30. Where was Omondi's mother on the day of the story? (1 mark)
   A. At the clinic getting her medicine
   B. At the market
   C. At school
   D. At the barber's

31. Which is the adverb form of 'happy'? (1 mark)
   A. happyly
   B. happly
   C. happily
   D. happiy

32. Which is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Mama, may I go to the shop.
   B. Mama, may I go to the shop?
   C. Mama may, I go to the shop?
   D. Mama may I go to the shop.

33. Which word means 'the leader of a team'? (1 mark)
   A. kit
   B. stadium
   C. whistle
   D. captain

34. Which is the best question for the answer 'In the school hall'? (1 mark)
   A. Where did they practise?
   B. Who practised?
   C. When did they practise?
   D. Whose hall is it?

35. Which words rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. clean and sweep
   B. tree and tall
   C. green and grass
   D. green and clean

36. Which is the past participle of 'break'? (1 mark)
   A. breaking
   B. broke
   C. broken
   D. breaked

37. What is a salary? (1 mark)
   A. Money borrowed from a bank
   B. Money paid to a worker regularly
   C. A school fee
   D. Money lost

38. Which sentence uses the pattern 'very ... but ...' correctly? (1 mark)
   A. Very shirt is nice, but.
   B. The shirt is very nice, but it is too expensive.
   C. The shirt very nice but expensive.
   D. The shirt is but very nice, it is expensive.

39. What is a headline? (1 mark)
   A. A photograph
   B. The writer's name
   C. A short bold title that tells what a news story is about
   D. An advert

40. What comes after a preposition in a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Another preposition
   B. A noun or pronoun
   C. A full stop
   D. A question mark

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give the meaning of each word and use it in a sentence: (a) harvest (b) fertilizer. (4 marks)

42. Why did the teacher say the prize message might be a trick? (3 marks)

43. Explain the meaning of 'tax' and 'fine'. (3 marks)

44. What kind of person is Kamau in 'The Clean-Up Day'? Give a reason from the text. (3 marks)

45. Arrange in order and write as a paragraph: (a) Finally, we went home. (b) We arrived at the farm at nine. (c) Then we fed the goats. (3 marks)

46. Plan a composition called 'My School Compound' by saying what goes into each of three paragraphs. (3 marks)

47. Make two sentences with 'very ... but ...' about shopping. (2 marks)

48. When is it right to interrupt a speaker, and how should you do it? (3 marks)

49. State three materials you can read for pleasure. (3 marks)

50. Rewrite in the past tense: 'Today we sweep the compound and plant a tree.' (2 marks)

51. Write one sentence using 'while' with the past progressive. (3 marks)

52. What lesson does the poem 'The Whistle' teach about winning and losing? (2 marks)

53. Explain the difference between a factual and an inferential question and give an example of each from the story. (4 marks)

54. Give one direct question and one indirect question about a story of a birthday party. (3 marks)

55. Explain the difference between 'my' and 'mine'. Use each in a sentence. (3 marks)

56. Describe how you would set up a reading club in your class. (4 marks)

57. Write four sentences using words with double consonants that you have learnt. (4 marks)

58. Write the short forms of: did not, she has, we will, let us. (4 marks)

59. Write two words for each cluster: (a) br (b) gr. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — differ in only one sound
   For example tin and din differ only in the first sound.

2. B — mother-in-law
   The mother of your husband or wife is your mother-in-law.

3. A — lake, rake
   Lake and rake differ only in the first sound.

4. D — invite
   Invite has /aɪ/ in its second syllable.

5. A — sleep very deeply
   A log does not move, so it means a deep sleep.

6. B — potatoes
   Some nouns ending in o add es.

7. A — pig, big
   Pig and big differ only in the first sound.

8. D — She returned it to its owner
   Neema found the woman and returned the purse.

9. B — intensive reading
   Intensive reading means careful, slow reading.

10. C — There is enough water to drink.
   Enough comes before the noun.

11. B — often or much
   A lot at the end of a sentence tells how much or how often.

12. B — lamb
   In lamb the b is not pronounced.

13. B — the first syllable
   The noun is PRE-sent and the verb is pre-SENT.

14. A — top
   North is shown at the top of a map.

15. B — Be polite, short and clear
   A good SMS is clear and polite.

16. B — food
   Food has /uː/. The others have /ʊ/.

17. A — worse
   Bad, worse, worst.

18. A — a message sent electronically
   Email stands for electronic mail.

19. A — the first syllable
   The noun is IN-crease and the verb is in-CREASE.

20. C — One wrong letter and the message will not reach the person
   The address decides where the message goes.

21. A — Compose
   They clicked Compose.

22. B — first, then, at last
   They are linking words for order.

23. D — yellow
   'Yellow' begins with /j/, the y sound. 'Jam' and 'giant' begin with /ʤ/.

24. D — chair
   'Chair' ends with the /ɛə/ sound.

25. C — dry season
   Seasons are common nouns and take small letters.

26. B — Close the door.
   Commands usually end with a full stop.

27. C — Vegetable peelings and dry leaves
   Compost heaps are made of peelings and dry leaves.

28. A — He doesn't work on the farm.
   After doesn't, the verb returns to its base form.

29. A — zebra
   'Zebra' begins with the buzzing /z/.

30. A — At the clinic getting her medicine
   The story says she was at the clinic.

31. C — happily
   Change y to i and add -ly.

32. B — Mama, may I go to the shop?
   A comma after the person addressed, and a question mark at the end.

33. D — captain
   The captain leads the team.

34. A — Where did they practise?
   The answer names a place.

35. D — green and clean
   'Green' and 'clean' end with the same sound.

36. C — broken
   Break, broke, broken.

37. B — Money paid to a worker regularly
   A salary is a regular payment for work.

38. B — The shirt is very nice, but it is too expensive.
   It has 'very' + adjective, then 'but' with the difficulty.

39. C — A short bold title that tells what a news story is about
   The headline gives the subject of a story.

40. B — A noun or pronoun
   For example: 'on the table'.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: (a) Harvest: to gather crops that are ready. We harvest maize in August. (b) Fertilizer: something added to soil to help plants grow. The farmer put fertilizer on the field.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each word: 1 for the meaning and 1 for a correct sentence.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: It promised a prize but asked for personal details, and some people send such messages to steal information.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for prize, 1 mark for details, 1 mark for stealing.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tax is money paid to the government to help run the country. A fine is money paid as a punishment for breaking a rule or law.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for showing a difference.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Observant and responsible: he noticed a hole in the fence and said it should be fixed at once.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each quality and 1 for evidence.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: We arrived at the farm at nine. Then we fed the goats. Finally, we went home.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sentence in the correct place.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Paragraph 1: what the compound is and where. Paragraph 2: details such as trees, playground, buildings. Paragraph 3: how I feel about it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each paragraph.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: The mango is very sweet, but it is small. The bag is very nice, but it is expensive.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: When you did not hear or understand, or someone needs urgent help. Say politely: 'Excuse me, may I say something?'
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the reasons and 1 for a polite phrase.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Story books, poems, magazines, comics, newspapers (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: Today we swept the compound and planted a tree.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for swept and 1 for planted.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Mother was cooking while I was doing my homework.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for while, 1 for was/were, 1 for verb-ing forms used correctly.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: To be a good sport: lose without crying, shake hands with the other team and say 'Good try'.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the lesson and 1 for a reason from the poem.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: A factual question has its answer stated in the text: 'Where was Omondi's mother?' An inferential question needs clues: 'How did Omondi feel at the start?'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for each example.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Direct: What time did the guests arrive? Indirect: Why do you think the girl was excited?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each question and 1 mark for correct types.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: My comes before a noun (This is my bag). Mine stands alone (The bag is mine).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sentence and 1 mark for the difference.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a day, time and place; give members roles; agree on rules such as taking turns; and read silently then share what was read.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four correct sentences with correctly spelt double consonant words.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: didn't, she's, we'll, let's
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

59. (4 marks)
   Answer: (a) bring, broom (or bread, brush) (b) green, grass (or grow, ground)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word.
